# When to choose what

For every step: the alternatives to what the platform chose, when each would win, and which approach fits which situation. Taken from section 9 and 10 of each chapter.

## [Step 1 · Repo, workspace and link to Project 0](../guide/step-01-repo-workspace-and-link-to-project-0.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| uv | Poetry, pip-tools | A team already standardised on them |
| just | make, Taskfile | `make` is everywhere; `just` has nicer syntax and no tab traps |
| SOPS + age | git-crypt, a dev-only Vault | Vault when developers already have short-lived access to it |
| Compose `external` network | A separate network with published ports | When Project A runs on a different host from Project 0 |
| Pattern secret scan | gitleaks, trufflehog | Larger repos; add them in CI (Step 38) |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Solo laptop with Project 0:** follow section 6 "On the Mac".
- **Cloud session or CI:** use the stand-in, and record every check that still needs the Mac.
- **Shared staging cluster:** the same provisioning scripts run as Kubernetes Jobs (Step 38).

## [Step 2 · Contracts and the component registry](../guide/step-02-contracts-and-component-registry.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract base classes | `typing.Protocol` | When you can't make implementations inherit (third-party classes) |
| Entry points | pluggy, stevedore | When you need hook ordering or plugin lifecycles |
| Pydantic v2 models | dataclasses, attrs | When validation and JSON Schema are not needed |
| Contract tests | Per-implementation tests only | Never for a safety property |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Adding an implementation of an existing slot:** follow `docs/how-to/add-a-component.md`.
- **A new kind of component:** it needs a new interface, a contract and an ADR; first check
  whether an existing slot fits.
- **Unit-testing a pattern:** use the dummies (`model_client.scripted`, `runtime_adapter.sequential`)
  rather than mocks.

## [Step 3 · The `agent.yaml` spec](../guide/step-03-the-agent-yaml-spec.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| YAML + Pydantic | Python-only definitions | Prototypes owned by one engineer |
| Generated JSON Schema | Hand-written schema | Never; it drifts |
| Unresolved secret refs | Env vars with secrets | Never for production: values leak into plans and traces |
| Required budgets | Optional budgets | Never; budgets are a safety default |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Deterministic process:** `autonomy: workflow`, `pattern: workflow`, a graph of function and
  tool nodes.
- **One tool-using assistant:** `autonomy: agent`, `pattern: react`, tools listed, budgets with
  tokens and cost.
- **Mixed process with an agentic step:** `autonomy: hybrid`, `pattern: hybrid`, an `agent` node
  inside the graph (like invoice-triage).
- **Teams of agents:** `autonomy: multi_agent`, `pattern: supervisor` (Phase E), `agents:` list.

## [Step 4 · Pattern compiler and runtime adapter skeleton](../guide/step-04-pattern-compiler-and-runtime-adapter.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Own plan format | Compile straight to LangGraph | A single-engine shop that will never switch |
| Compile-time approvals | Runtime-only approval checks | Never alone; Step 10 adds policy-time checks *as well* |
| OTLP to the Collector | Direct Langfuse SDK | Never; vendor lock-in (ADR 0010) |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Explicit process:** `pattern: workflow` with a graph.
- **Process with agentic steps:** `pattern: hybrid` and `agent` nodes; each agent node's
  `pattern` must have a builder installed (`react` arrives in Step 13).
- **State-driven process (statuses and transitions):** `pattern: state_machine`.

## [Step 5 · Model access per role](../guide/step-05-model-access-per-role.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway for every call | Direct provider SDK | Only behind an ADR, e.g. a feature the gateway can't proxy |
| httpx client | OpenAI SDK | If we needed APIs beyond chat completions |
| One repair attempt | Constrained decoding only | When every model supports strict JSON mode reliably |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Planning, judging:** a stronger alias behind `planner` / `judge`.
- **Routing, summarising:** a fast, cheap alias behind `router` / `summariser`.
- **A spec needing a special model for one role:** override it in the spec's `models:`.

## [Step 6 · Tool contract and registry](../guide/step-06-tool-contract-and-registry.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres registry | In-memory | Single-process tests |
| Valkey idempotency | Postgres table | When Valkey isn't available; slower claims |
| S3 spill | Truncate only | Never for audit: the full output must be retrievable |
| JSON Schema checks | Pydantic models per tool | Python-only tools; MCP tools arrive as JSON Schema anyway |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Lookups and searches:** `read`, `idempotent: true`, a retry policy.
- **Drafts, tickets, comments:** `write`; the runtime supplies the key.
- **Payments, deletions, external emails:** `irreversible`; approval in the spec; no retries.

## [Step 7 · MCP client](../guide/step-07-mcp-client.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Official SDK | Hand-written JSON-RPC | Never; the protocol moves quickly |
| Allowlist | Open discovery | Never in production |
| OAuth client credentials | Static bearer token | Short-lived experiments with a server that can't do OAuth |
| Direct client | Everything via the platform gateway | Step 8 adds the gateway so all traffic shares one policy point |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Vendor or internal server under review:** `trusted: true`, still with `allowed_tools`.
- **Community server:** `trusted: false`, explicit `side_effects`, minimal `allowed_tools`, pinned version.
- **Older server that can't handle probes:** `protocol: legacy` (or let `auto` fall back).

## [Step 8 · Platform MCP server (the gateway)](../guide/step-08-platform-mcp-server.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway | Direct client-to-server | Trusted internal tools on the same host, behind an ADR |
| Token exchange | Forward the user token | Never |
| OPA | Cerbos (Step 10 adds it as an option) | Teams preferring YAML policies |
| Group-path tenants | A `tenant` claim | If Project 0 already issues one |

**Which fits which situation**

- **External MCP clients (developers, other teams):** connect to the gateway's `/mcp`.
- **Platform agents:** use the same gateway (Step 13 onwards), so their calls share policy and audit.
- **A new downstream service that needs user permissions:** add it to
  `infra/provision/keycloak.yaml` and call it through `TokenExchanger`.

## [Step 9 · Sandboxed code execution](../guide/step-09-sandboxed-code-execution.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| gVisor | Kata Containers | KVM hosts needing VM isolation behind the same Docker interface; verified in CI |
| gVisor | Firecracker | Untrusted code with a high blast radius; a whole microVM per run; verified in CI |
| gVisor | Managed sandbox service | No infrastructure to run; stub by decision until a vendor passes privacy and residency review (ADR 0021) |
| Docker CLI | Kubernetes pods with `RuntimeClass: gvisor` | Production (Step 38) |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Laptop / CI:** gVisor via Docker.
- **Kubernetes production:** gVisor RuntimeClass (GKE Sandbox on Google Cloud), sandbox pods on a
  dedicated node pool.
- **Strict multi-tenant isolation on KVM hardware:** Kata or Firecracker.

## [Step 10 · Tool authorisation](../guide/step-10-tool-authorisation.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| OPA (Rego) | Cerbos (YAML + CEL) | Your teams already run Cerbos or prefer YAML policies; implemented, parity-tested |
| Rego data for groups | OpenFGA relationships | Per-object sharing (owners, teams, delegations) at scale; implemented |
| Fixed one-minute window | Token bucket or sliding window | Billing-grade or very smooth limits |
| Token exchange per audience | Forwarding the user's token | Never: it hands a broad token to every service |
| Per-call MCP connection for on-behalf-of | Per-user connection pool | Latency-sensitive, high-volume tools |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Default (Mac and most deployments):** OPA from Project 0, no extra services.
- **Company standard is Cerbos:** `MCP_GATEWAY_PDP=cerbos`; keep the parity test green.
- **Objects shared by owner or team (invoices, cases, documents):** add `+openfga`, list the
  tools in `relations.yaml`, and have the owning application write the relationships.
- **High-risk agents:** risk tier `high`; every write then needs approval and irreversible
  actions need two people.
- **Incident:** flip the kill switch for the tenant or agent in `data.json` and reload.

## [Step 11 · Runtime adapter](../guide/step-11-runtime-adapter.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| LangGraph (default) | Microsoft Agent Framework | Microsoft-centred estates (Azure, .NET agents); implemented and contract-tested |
| LangGraph | OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI, Google ADK | Agent-loop-first designs; built with the agent patterns in Step 13 |
| LangGraph | CrewAI | Role-based "crew" prototypes; stub (catalogue) |
| Memory checkpoints | Postgres / Temporal | Anything beyond tests: Steps 18 and 19 |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Most agents and workflows:** LangGraph.
- **Organisation standardised on Microsoft's agent stack:** `adapter: agent_framework`.
- **Very long runs (hours to days) or exactly-once side effects:** Temporal durability (Step 19),
  whichever adapter runs the steps.
- **Evaluating a new engine:** implement the adapter, pass `WorkflowRuntimeContract`, then run
  the same-spec test against it.

## [Step 12 · Deterministic workflows](../guide/step-12-deterministic-workflows.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Platform saga | Engine-native compensation (Temporal) | Very long runs; Step 19 reuses the same `compensation:` declarations |
| Journal replay | Engine checkpoint "time travel" (LangGraph) | Debugging one engine interactively |
| `string.Template` value paths | Jinja2 templates | Rich formatting needs; at the cost of a code surface |
| Workflow | Agent (Step 13) | The steps or their order cannot be known in advance |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Known steps, known order:** workflow (`pattern: workflow`).
- **Known steps with one judgement call:** workflow with a router or LLM node.
- **Writes to several external systems:** give every write a `compensation`.
- **Shared sub-process (KYC, approval chain):** a `subgraph` node.
- **Unknown steps:** an agent pattern (Step 13), possibly inside a workflow (`pattern: hybrid`).

## [Step 13 · Single tool-calling agent](../guide/step-13-single-tool-calling-agent.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Native loop | OpenAI Agents SDK engine | Teams standardised on the Agents SDK's style; no approvals inside the loop |
| Native loop | Pydantic AI engine | Typed, Pydantic-first codebases; no approvals inside the loop |
| Native loop | Google ADK (A2A service, Step 21) | Google-centred estates; agents published over A2A |
| Native tool calling | Text ReAct | Models without tool calling |
| ReAct | Plan-and-execute, ReWOO, reflection (Step 14) | Longer tasks where planning first saves steps or cost |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Fixed steps:** a workflow (Step 12), not an agent.
- **A few tools, open-ended question:** `pattern: react` with the native loop.
- **Agent that may move money or message customers:** native loop with `approval` on those tools,
  risk tier `medium` or `high`.
- **Small local model without tool calling:** text ReAct is chosen automatically.
- **Existing Agents SDK or Pydantic AI code:** the matching engine, after it passes the contract.

## [Step 14 · Planning and reflection](../guide/step-14-planning-and-reflection.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Plan-and-execute | ReAct | Short tasks, or steps that depend heavily on what tools return |
| ReWOO | Plan-and-execute | Tool results may change the plan |
| Reflection (self) | Evaluator-optimiser (`judge`) | The drafting model is weak at judging its own work |
| `planner.llm` | A rules-based planner (your own component) | The steps are known; skip the model call |
| Strategies on one node | A workflow (Step 12) | The steps are fixed in advance and need per-step approvals or saga undo |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Two or three tool calls, open-ended:** `react`.
- **Several tool calls whose order is clear from the question:** `rewoo`.
- **Longer tasks where a step might fail:** `plan_execute`.
- **Writing where quality matters more than speed:** `evaluator_optimiser` with a `judge` role.
- **Quick polish of a short answer on a capable model:** `reflection`.
- **Anything that moves money or messages customers:** `react` with approvals, or a workflow.

## [Step 15 · Routing, chaining and hybrid](../guide/step-15-routing-chaining-and-hybrid.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| LLM router | Embedding router | High volume, stable topics, good examples; lower cost per request |
| LLM router | Rules router | Fixed vocabulary (form codes, product names); zero cost and full predictability |
| Gate on the step | Separate check step (function node) | The check needs other steps' results or external data |
| Prompt chain | Workflow (Step 12) | Steps branch or run in parallel |
| Router pattern | Supervisor (Step 22) | The handlers need to talk to each other or be re-delegated |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Support inbox, a few clear topics, lots of traffic:** embedding router with a fallback to a
  person.
- **Messy free-text requests, low volume:** LLM router with route descriptions.
- **Structured codes or keywords:** rules router.
- **Extract, transform, then write:** prompt chain with a gate after each LLM step.
- **Routine cases plus exceptions that need judgement:** hybrid, with an agent only on the
  exception path (as invoice-triage does).
- **Anything irreversible:** an approval in front of it; the evidence makes it run only as
  approved.

## [Step 16 · Agentic RAG](../guide/step-16-agentic-rag.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Agentic RAG | Naive RAG (one search) | Single-document questions; lowest cost and latency |
| Agentic RAG | ReAct with the search tool (Step 13) | Mixed tasks where search is one tool among many |
| Self-check by the same role | A separate `judge` role | The answering model is weak at judging itself |
| rag-core `naive` per hop | `graph` or `sql` architectures | Relationship-heavy or tabular questions |

**Which fits which situation**

- **"What does policy X say?"**: naive RAG or agentic RAG with `max_hops: 1`.
- **"Who approves Y for team Z?"** (policy plus org chart): agentic RAG.
- **Questions over structured data (amounts, counts):** allow the `sql` architecture.
- **Sensitive documents:** nothing extra in the spec; access is enforced by rag-core from the
  user's token, and citations can only come from what that user retrieved.

## [Step 17 · Run API and streaming](../guide/step-17-run-api-and-streaming.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| SSE | WebSocket (`/v1/runs/{id}/ws`) | Clients that already hold a socket, or need to send messages back on the same connection |
| AG-UI events | Custom JSON | Never for new UIs; only for a legacy client that cannot change |
| Our minimal page | An AG-UI client library (e.g. CopilotKit) | Product UIs; the API is the same |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A web app showing an agent's progress:** SSE with `fetch`, reconnecting with `after`.
- **A back-end service starting runs:** create with an idempotency key, then poll state or follow
  events.
- **An approvals inbox:** list runs waiting on your group (the interrupt names it), then post a
  decision as yourself.
- **Long human waits:** fine for now, but keep the run's service up until Step 18 makes runs
  durable.

## [Step 18 · Checkpoints and threads](../guide/step-18-checkpoints-and-threads.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres checkpoints | Valkey | Local development where losing state is acceptable |
| Postgres checkpoints | SQLite / memory | Unit tests |
| Platform checkpoints | An engine's own checkpointer | Features only that engine offers (not needed so far) |
| Checkpoint per node | Durable workflows on Temporal (Step 19) | Runs that wait days, need timers and signals at scale |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Anything with write or irreversible tools:** Postgres checkpoints, always.
- **Quick experiments on a laptop:** memory or Valkey.
- **Customer support case that needs a "what if":** fork the thread at the checkpoint before the
  decision and run it again.
- **Data that must be deleted after N days:** set retention to N days; keep the newest few per
  active thread.

## [Step 19 · Durable long runs on Temporal](../guide/step-19-durable-long-runs-on-temporal.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal | Step 18 checkpoints | Runs of minutes with no long waits: less to operate |
| Temporal | Restate (stub) | Request/response services that need durable steps and a light server |
| Temporal | DBOS (stub) | Only Postgres is allowed and no extra server can be run |
| Values by reference | Inline values | Small values (under 256 KiB), which is most of them |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Invoice approval that can take a week:** Temporal, with the 7-day timer and expiry on the
  error path.
- **Chat assistant answering in seconds:** checkpoints (Step 18); Temporal adds nothing.
- **Nightly batch of thousands of documents:** Temporal, so workers can be added or lost
  freely.
- **Team that can only run Postgres:** Step 18 checkpoints now; DBOS once it is implemented.

## [Step 20 · Long-term memory](../guide/step-20-long-term-memory.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| pgvector | Qdrant | Vectors already in Qdrant, or a dedicated vector engine at larger scale |
| pgvector | Mem0 (library) | Teams using Mem0's API and its keyword plus vector search |
| pgvector | Zep, Letta (stubs) | Only if the owner accepts a cloud service: Zep CE is unsupported and Letta's server is retired |
| `validating` policy | `human_curated` | Regulated domains where a person approves every memory |
| `validating` policy | `read_only` | Agents that may use curated memory but never write |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Customer assistant that should learn preferences:** `scope: user`, `remember` tool,
  `validating` policy.
- **Team knowledge shared across users:** `scope: tenant`, written by people
  (`human_curated`), not by agents.
- **Agent that reads documents all day:** keep `validating`. It will refuse what the documents
  say, by design.
- **Strict privacy or regulated data:** pgvector with encryption, short `ttl_days`, and erasure
  wired to the data lifecycle.

## [Step 21 · Context engineering](../guide/step-21-context-engineering.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| `rolling_summary` | `trim` | Short sessions, where losing the oldest turns does not matter and no summariser cost is wanted |
| `rolling_summary` | `offload_s3` | Tool-heavy runs with large results that must stay recoverable |
| LLM summariser | Extractive | No model budget, or the strictest poisoning stance |
| Just-in-time tools | All tools every call | Fewer than about 20 tools |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Customer chat that runs for hours:** `rolling_summary` with the LLM summariser. Add Step 20
  memory for facts that must outlive the session.
- **Research agent reading many documents:** `rolling_summary` plus compaction. Raise
  `compact_tool_results_over` if documents are short.
- **Ops agent with 100+ tools:** just-in-time tools, with a lower `jit_top_k` if the model gets
  confused.
- **Regulated, strict anti-poisoning:** the `extractive` summariser.

## [Step 22 · Supervisor and hierarchical teams](../guide/step-22-supervisor-and-hierarchical-teams.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| LLM dispatcher | Rules dispatcher | The order is fixed (research, then analysis, then writing): cheaper and predictable |
| Supervisor team | One agent with all tools | Small tasks with low risk and few tools |
| Supervisor team | Handoff or group chat (Step 23) | Control should pass between peers rather than through a coordinator |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Report from research plus figures:** a supervisor with researcher, analyst and writer, and
  the rules dispatcher once the order is stable.
- **Open-ended investigations:** the LLM dispatcher with a tight `max_rounds` and team budget.
- **Large organisations:** hierarchical teams, where a department supervisor is a worker of a
  top supervisor, with `max_depth` set.
- **Sensitive tools:** give them to one worker only, with approvals on that worker's spec.

## [Step 23 · Handoff, group chat, parallel and debate](../guide/step-23-handoff-group-chat-parallel-and-debate.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Handoff | Supervisor (Step 22) | A coordinator should see the whole task and decide each step |
| Group chat | Reflection in one agent (Step 14) | One agent can critique itself well enough |
| Map-reduce | A loop in a workflow | Few items, or each depends on the previous |
| Debate | A single judge-model check | The answer needs checking rather than arguing |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Customer support routing:** handoff with explicit allowed edges.
- **Drafting with review:** a group chat of writer and critic, with `answer_from: writer`.
- **Summarising a batch of documents:** map-reduce, with `concurrency` matched to the gateway's
  rate limits.
- **Policy or design decisions:** a debate with a judge, and few rounds.

## [Step 24 · A2A server and client](../guide/step-24-a2a-server-and-client.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Separate gateway | A2A inside the run API | Very small deployments where one fewer service matters more than isolation |
| Pinned card keys | Trust the card's `jku` key URL | A trusted agent registry vouches for keys (Step 25) |
| Official `a2a-sdk` | Pydantic AI `to_a2a()` (FastA2A) | Publishing a single Pydantic AI agent quickly, without card signing or platform policy |
| JSON-RPC / HTTP+JSON | gRPC | High-volume calls between services that already run gRPC |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A partner company's agent:** list it with pinned keys and `on_behalf_of`, so it sees only
  what the user may see.
- **Another internal platform:** client credentials, and a narrow OPA rule for its client ID.
- **A public read-only agent:** `auth: none`, `side_effect: read` only if it truly cannot
  change anything.
- **Agents in the same process:** don't use A2A; use a team pattern (Steps 22–23).

## [Step 25 · Agent registry and discovery](../guide/step-25-agent-registry-and-discovery.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres registry | Backstage catalogue in Git | Your organisation already discovers services in Backstage and approves through pull requests |
| Separate approval step | Status inside `agent.yaml` | Never for production: authors would approve their own agents |
| Gate in the API and worker | OPA rule with registry data | Registry data is already bundled into OPA (useful for the kill-switch drill) |
| SQLite locally | In-memory | Tests, where nothing should persist |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A developer trying a new agent:** `dev`, where drafts run.
- **A release to staging:** run its evals, then `just agents --approve ... --expires`.
- **An agent being replaced:** approve the new version, then deprecate the old one; retire it
  once nothing uses it.
- **A Backstage shop:** `AGENT_REGISTRY=backstage`, with approvals as reviewed pull requests to
  `catalog/agents`.

## [Step 26 · Budgets and loop control](../guide/step-26-budgets-and-loop-control.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Stop | Stop and summarise | People read the partial result and need a quick account of it |
| In-process budgets plus gateway ceiling | A gateway key per run | You need exact cross-process spend per run and can afford a key per run |
| Progress-aware loop detection | Repeat counting only | Agents never poll, so any repeat is a loop |
| Shared circuit breakers | Retries only | Dependencies fail briefly and recover in seconds |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Customer-facing assistant:** a cost and wall-clock limit, and `stop`; show the reason to
  the user.
- **Back-office batch:** `summarise`, so reviewers see what was done before the limit.
- **Agent that writes to systems:** `max_calls_per_tool` of 1 on the writing tool.
- **Teams:** keep `max_delegation_depth` small and put the team budget on the team spec.

## [Step 27 · Guardrails](../guide/step-27-guardrails.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Rules + classifier | LLM judge | Subtle attacks where context matters, and the extra model call is affordable |
| Quarantine untrusted content | Stop the run | Highly sensitive agents where any sign of attack must halt the work |
| Presidio (Project 0) | Cloud DLP | You already use a cloud DLP service and accept sending text to it |
| Guardrails in the platform | Gateway-only guardrails | Only model traffic matters, with no tools or retrieval |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Agents that read the web or customer documents:** `prompt_injection` with the classifier,
  plus approvals on any write.
- **Agents that answer customers:** `pii_redaction` on output, plus `output_schema` with
  forbidden promises.
- **Agents that move money:** `tool_args_schema` limits plus approvals (Step 28).
- **Internal research agents:** the baseline, plus a topic filter if they must stay in scope.

## [Step 28 · Human-in-the-loop](../guide/step-28-human-in-the-loop.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Interrupts in the run API (short waits) | Temporal signals (long waits) | Approvals that may take days, across deployments and restarts at scale |
| Cancel on expiry | Auto-reject and continue | The agent has a sensible "not approved" path to take |
| Desk inside the run API | A separate approvals service | Several platforms share one reviewer inbox |
| Two-person by policy | One approver with a higher role | Small teams where two people aren't available |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Payments:** the finance group, an edit allowed (amounts), two people at high risk, and a
  short SLA.
- **Customer emails:** approval with edits to the text, plus review-after sampling.
- **Data deletion:** two-person, no edits, and expiry cancels.
- **Stuck or confused agents:** operator take-over, with the handover state for the person
  finishing the work.

## [Step 29 · Agent identity and secrets](../guide/step-29-agent-identity-and-secrets.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| OpenBao | HashiCorp Vault (same API) | Vault Enterprise is already the company standard |
| OpenBao | Cloud IAM and secret managers (stubs) | You run on one cloud: AWS STS or RDS IAM auth, GCP service-account tokens, Azure managed identity |
| AppRole for the runtime | SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity (stub) | Kubernetes, where each pod can prove what it is without a secret |
| Dynamic credentials | Static secrets in KV, rotated | The target system can't create short-lived users or tokens |
| Two-hop delegation | One platform identity for everything | Never for agents that act for users. Acceptable for a single-purpose internal job |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Agents that read business databases:** `sql_read` with named queries and a read-only
  credential role.
- **Agents that call services for a user (rag-core, MCP servers, A2A partners):** on-behalf-of
  auth. Delegation through the agent happens automatically.
- **Batch agents with no user:** the agent's own identity only. Grant credentials, not user
  audiences.
- **Cloud deployment:** keep the contracts, and finish the cloud broker for your provider in
  Step 37.

## [Step 30 · Agent telemetry, metrics and SLOs](../guide/step-30-agent-telemetry-metrics-and-slos.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Langfuse for content | Arize Phoenix (OTLP) | Your team already runs Phoenix; it's another OTLP target with content |
| Platform-owned instrumentation | OpenLLMetry / OpenInference auto-instrumentation | Agents written outside the platform that you can't wrap |
| Prometheus rules | Grafana-managed alerts | Alerting is centralised in Grafana and promtool tests aren't needed |
| Multi-window burn-rate paging | Static error thresholds | Very low traffic, where ratios swing too much |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Debugging one bad run:** the Tempo trace for timing and where it failed, then Langfuse for
  what the model saw and said (redacted).
- **"Are we OK?":** the **Agent platform** dashboard: success ratio, p95, tool errors, approvals.
- **Money:** cost per tenant and per run, budget trips, and `just cost-reconcile` (Step 26).
- **Attacks:** guardrail hits and the guardrail-blocks runbook, then the audit log for the runs.

## [Step 31 · Agent audit trail](../guide/step-31-agent-audit-trail.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Postgres trail with triggers and a chain | S3 Object Lock or immudb (WORM) | A regulator requires write-once storage |
| One chain | A chain per tenant | Audit volume makes the single lock a bottleneck |
| Digest plus redacted arguments | Full arguments, encrypted | Investigators need full content and an erasure process exists outside the chain |
| Own trail behind `AuditSink` | Project 0's audit service directly | Once its schema and API are verified on the Mac |

**Which fits which situation**

- **"Was anything changed?":** `just audit-verify`, on a schedule and before any audit export.
- **"What did this run do?":** `just audit-replay <run>`, then the trace id in Tempo and Langfuse
  for timing and (redacted) content.
- **"Who approved this payment?":** the `approval.decided` event's `by` and `calls` digest,
  matched to the `tool.call`.
- **Local development:** no `AGENT_AUDIT_DSN`, so each service keeps a JSONL trail that
  `just audit-verify --file` checks.

## [Step 32 · Governance artefacts](../guide/step-32-governance-artefacts.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Generated cards | Hand-written model cards | Never for live systems; fine for a one-off research model |
| CI gate by tier | Code-owner review on every path | Separate teams own different tiers |
| Python gate | Conftest/OPA over the diff | OPA is already the CI policy tool for this |
| Register in the repo | A GRC tool (ServiceNow, OneTrust) | The organisation already keeps its register there; export `cards/register.yaml` to it |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A reviewer asks "what does this agent touch?":** its agent card.
- **An incident:** the audit event's `spec_hash` → lineage → the exact prompts, models and tools.
- **A compliance review:** the AI-use register and the system cards.
- **Changing a high-risk agent:** open a pull request; the check names who must approve.

## [Step 33 · Testing pyramid](../guide/step-33-testing-pyramid.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Interface-level cassettes | VCR.py at the HTTP layer | Testing an HTTP client itself |
| In-repo network guard | pytest-socket | You want its finer per-test allow lists |
| In-process chaos | Toxiproxy, Chaos Mesh | Real clusters, network partitions (Step 37) |
| Gateway fallbacks | Platform-side fallback lists | No gateway in front of the models |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A new component:** a contract test, plus unit tests with the scripted model.
- **A new agent or prompt:** record a cassette against the stand-in, and replay it in CI.
- **A new MCP server:** an `McpToolContract` subclass.
- **"What happens when X is down?":** a chaos test faking X's transport or clock.
- **Before a release:** `just test-integration` on the full stand-in.

## [Step 34 · Agent evaluation harness](../guide/step-34-agent-evaluation-harness.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Checks over platform records | Final-text scoring (Promptfoo, OpenAI Evals) | Single-prompt features with no tools or policy |
| Generated tasks | Curated production samples | Once production traffic exists: add them alongside |
| Rubric judge with human calibration | Pairwise preference judging | Comparing two versions' writing quality head to head |
| Mechanics baseline now | Quality baseline only | Real models are available in CI |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A prompt or model change:** run the app on real models, `eval-compare` against the baseline,
  and read the regressions.
- **A platform change:** `just eval-baseline-check`, which CI runs.
- **"Is the writing any good?":** the rubric judge, once it has been calibrated against people.
- **A release decision (Step 38):** the published real-model results on the card.

## [Step 35 · Simulation and red-teaming](../guide/step-35-simulation-and-red-teaming.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Obedient adversary for scenarios | A real model as the attacker's target | Measuring a specific model's resistance (done by the libraries) |
| Fixed promptfoo library in CI | promptfoo's generated red team everywhere | When a local generator model is available in CI |
| garak with string detectors | garak's model-based detectors (toxicity, misleading claims) | When detector models can be downloaded and pinned |
| Issues per fingerprint | A findings dashboard only | Very large finding volumes, where issues become noise |
| Block on high/critical | Block on any finding | Very high-risk deployments, where the threshold can be lowered in the gate |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Changing a control** (policy, guardrail, approval, sandbox): run `just redteam`. CI also
  runs it on every push.
- **Changing or swapping a model:** run the attack libraries with
  `AGENT_REDTEAM_PROVIDER=gateway` on the Mac.
- **A new tool or app:** add a scenario attack for its riskiest action and a canary.
- **Before a release:** `release.yml` runs everything and applies the gate.
- **Debugging a flaky multi-turn behaviour:** replay with the same simulator profile and seed.

## [Step 36 · CI eval gates](../guide/step-36-ci-eval-gates.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline-relative checks on every PR | Absolute floors on every PR | When CI has real models |
| Review-based approval | A label | When approvals don't need to be tied to a commit |
| Gate inside the integration job | A separate workflow | When the stack is cheap to start, or gates run elsewhere |
| Affected apps only on PRs | Every app on every PR | Small repositories where the full run is fast |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A prompt or spec change to one app:** the PR gates that app, and the comment shows the
  result.
- **A shared library or model change:** every app is gated.
- **A deliberate trade (more cost for better results):** re-record the baseline if needed, and
  get `/approve-cost` from an approver.
- **Before a release:** `release.yml` runs every gate and the full red team.

## [Step 37 · Threat model and compliance](../guide/step-37-threat-model-and-compliance.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Checked YAML | Threat Dragon or pytm diagrams | Larger teams who want visual modelling; keep the checker for the links |
| STRIDE per component | Attack trees per goal | Deep analysis of one high-value asset, such as payments |
| Coarse, verified framework mapping | Full clause-by-clause mapping | When the standards and legal review are at hand |
| API-applied retention | Database jobs | Bulk archives outside the platform's own data |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A new component or data store:** add it with its boundary, a STRIDE pass and tests before it
  ships.
- **A new tool with side effects:** add or extend the threat (tool misuse, tampering) and its
  red-team scenario.
- **A data request from a person:** export or erase through the API; both are audited.
- **An audit or customer questionnaire:** start from the control matrix and the compliance
  sources page.

## [Step 38 · Environments and promotion](../guide/step-38-environments-and-promotion.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Kustomize | Helm | Packaging the platform for others to install with many options |
| Argo CD | Flux | A team already running Flux; same GitOps model |
| Agent-level canary in the run API | Argo Rollouts (image-level canary) | Canarying the platform's own code rather than an agent version; both can coexist |
| KEDA on the Temporal backlog | HPA on CPU | Work that is CPU-bound rather than queue-bound |
| Run leases in Postgres | Sticky sessions at the load balancer | One region, few replicas, and acceptance that a lost replica stops its runs until restart |
| WAL archiving and PITR | Nightly logical dumps | Small, rarely written data where a day of loss is acceptable |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A prompt or model change to an agent:** a new version, staging, then a 10% canary.
- **A risky change you can't afford to show anyone yet:** a shadow candidate (no side effects,
  nothing shown), then a canary.
- **Switching off an agent or one of its tools quickly:** a feature flag in the releases file;
  in an emergency, the kill switch (Step 10).
- **A platform code change:** `just deploy-images` to a commit's images, through a pull request.
- **Data loss or corruption:** `docs/runbooks/dr-restore.md`.

## [Step 39 · Reuse kit](../guide/step-39-reuse-kit.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| Copier | Cookiecutter | You never need to update projects from a newer template |
| A project per team, running the platform from a pinned base | One shared platform hosting all agents | Agents made only of specs and MCP tools, with no team code |
| Git pin of the SDK | A private package index | Many teams and frequent releases; an index makes versions easier to browse |
| `pattern: custom` + `components.pattern_builder` | An open string for `pattern` | Never here: the closed list keeps validation precise |
| In-process run API for `agentctl run` | A local docker compose of the platform | Debugging something that needs Postgres, Temporal or Keycloak; then use `--api` |

**Which fits which situation**

- **A team with its own tools or steps:** a project from the template.
- **An agent built only from platform tools and MCP servers:** a spec in the platform's
  `agents/` may be enough.
- **Calling the platform from an existing application:** the run API (`docs/reference/endpoints.md`).
- **Calling it from another agent framework:** A2A or MCP, same reference.
- **A new reasoning pattern:** a `PatternBuilder` in the team's package, `pattern: custom`.
- **A domain-specific quality check:** an evaluator, named in the golden tasks' `expected.custom`.

## [Step 40 · Reference apps and wrap-up](../guide/step-40-reference-apps.md)

| Choice | Alternative | When the alternative wins |
|---|---|---|
| A team with a critic for the report | One agent with a checklist | If real-model runs show no gain from the team (ADR 0051's rule) |
| A nested spec as its own agent | Children sharing the parent's model and tools | Never: it breaks least privilege |
| A generated results table | A hand-written table | Never here: numbers drift from their runs |
| `publish_report` as a platform tool | Publishing through an MCP server | When reports go to a real document system with its own API |

**Which fits which situation**

- **Answers from documents, with sources:** agentic RAG (knowledge-assistant).
- **Work that splits into roles, where review matters:** a supervisor team as a subgraph, with
  a critic and an approval before anything leaves (research-report).
- **Mostly fixed rules with exceptions:** hybrid, with functions for the rules and an agent only
  for the exceptions (invoice-triage).
- **Anything irreversible:** mark the tool `irreversible`. The platform makes it wait for a
  person.
